item.title: Re: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Responded:

+ show block
– hide block

They don't. They simply try to manufacture Objects that could aid the foundation, who would then in turn be classified as Thaumiel.

Not all objects that could be helpful are given the Thaumiel class. If this person is only churning out items that would be considered Thaumiel, that's a difficult to believe level of specificity and ability.

This is the reason this individual does not speak to the foundation at all while building the factory. They want the products to speak for themselves.

Again, why would they assume the Foundation would use the products to begin with, especially if they don't have any insight into the production and motive behind the items?

he thinks that the foundation in its entirety is completely good and would never do anything evil.

Given that the Foundation would have had to be ridiculously sloppy in order for the person to witness a single event that makes them understand that there's a whole shadow organization that is intent on containing the anomalous, this is difficult to believe. You as the author inherently know everything ahead of time, but your character needs to learn in a believable manner if you want the audience to take the story seriously.

This Person does not happen to have it. He builds it himself. How he does that is something I am still working on. Plan is currently that he uses his money to hire people that know a thing or two and compiles their knowledge.

The issue with this is that it's overpowered and contrived. You have so many unlikely elements already, the fact that the guy inherits money, the fact that he wasn't noticed by the Foundation during a containment event, the fact that he hires people to make anomalies somehow, and so on. Each of these traits separately is already potentially skepticism-raising; combining so many of these coincidences just makes for a story that feels sloppily made up and fake.

things he thinks are useful like gloves that make your hands indestructable, boxes that lock things inside with no way of opening them from the inside, glasses that protect your mind from seeing things and hazmat suits to keep nasty stuff away.

Since none of these things can be reliably used to observably contain anomalies, they wouldn't be classified as Thaumiel.

I want the factory to have 1 important person in charge, who hired other people to help him build it, yet him pulling all the strings.

This doesn't answer my question of why you want only one person.

I am open to any changes that make the story better/clearer without completely changing its direction.

I feel like for this to stand more of a chance with the audience, you need to change the following:

  • don't have just one person in charge. Have at least two or three friends/family members. If you just have one person, they'll seem like a too-important overpowered Mary Sue character.
  • don't have them witness a Foundation containment and somehow go unnoticed. Have someone they are close to be involved in an incident, and maybe taken into Foundation custody. When the person goes looking, they find a Foundation agent checking up on the amnesticized someone and the agent gives some very brief information about being with an organization that "helps after disasters" or something. Your character talks to their friend/whoever who was in the incident, and wants to start helping the people who saved their friend/whoever. This will make more sense than your current setup.
  • don't have the setup be for a factory, which implies mass production and cut corners for many exact copies of the same product. Use "workshop" or the like. This will make the Foundation more interested in testing the items as individual anomalies rather than just locking all of the stuff up as repeat junk.

There will definitely be more changes needed after these, but that's what I would start with.

item.title: Re: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for taking a look at my concept yet again.

+ show block
– hide block

My answers:

how would they know what Thaumiel class is?

They don't. They simply try to manufacture Objects that could aid the foundation, who would then in turn be classified as Thaumiel.

Why would they assume Foundation personnel would trust their products

This is the reason this individual does not speak to the foundation at all while building the factory. They want the products to speak for themselves.

let alone pay for them?

Since this concept would have been to long if I included details about the individual i left them out. This individual inherits a vast amount of money from their dead family members. This money will be used to set everything necessary up. They have a genuine good heart and witnesses the foundation helping humans against an anomaly. Since he is not directly from the foundation he does not know of the inner workings and events, i.e. he thinks that the foundation in its entirety is completely good and would never do anything evil.
With that in mind, he tries to fabricate objects that would help them while also receiving money in return for his work. He doesn't even think about the foundation ceasing his property. Since his family is quite rich he has always been taught that money is his highest priority and he follows those teachings.

It's already a stretch of disbelief for me to believe that the Foundation just happened to not notice this person witnessing a containment incident

That makes sense, but I also find it hard to believe that the foundation catches every single person that witnesses a containment incident. Someone will slip by somehow eventually but this time it's a nice person.

and said person just happens to have the factory means to produce anomalies somehow

This Person does not happen to have it. He builds it himself. How he does that is something I am still working on. Plan is currently that he uses his money to hire people that know a thing or two and compiles their knowledge.

When you add in the fact that they somehow learned enough about the Foundation to figure out the kind of anomalies that would be considered useful

I have thought about that part. Since he himself would be confronted with anomalies or at least some knowledge of them he would know some dangers, like looking at them or directly touching them. He is building a abnormal factory after all. So the stuff he would produce are things he thinks are useful like gloves that make your hands indestructable, boxes that lock things inside with no way of opening them from the inside, glasses that protect your mind from seeing things and hazmat suits to keep nasty stuff away.

Since this individual has knowledge on how to construct a factory and knowledge of the abnormal, I dont think this is too far fetched. Also he has no direct contact to the foundation. That is the reason he programs a virus that randomly infects printers etc. to print that messages because he knows the foundation will pick up the signal and find him. He has not done so sooner because he wanted his products to be finished before contacting them.

Why do you want the factory to be the work of one person?

I want the factory to have 1 important person in charge, who hired other people to help him build it, yet him pulling all the strings.

Why do you want them to just randomly and conveniently find out a lot of information about the Foundation, thereby making the Foundation look incompetent in terms of information security?

I dont want to do that. I want 1 single mistake from the foundation and 1 single rich person with a good heart and a too naive way of thinking to clash and culminate into this story.

their scheme is disturbed by something as mundane as a coal company

The coal company part is definetely something that could get changed, but I don't think it is huge problem. The individual needs money to build up his little factory and the coal company makes prices go up by buying all needed materials in the area, thereby making it more expensive for him to buy said materials. Also, he still is a good person that abides by the rules and just ignores it. His money eventually runs low and he begins to sell businesses that his family own that gave him money in the first place in order to fullfill his current dream. He risks it all and gets nothing because he is too naive and simple minded.

How open are you to changing these elements to make the story more believable and the main character more of a relatable individual and not an excessively exceptional caricature?

I am open to any changes that make the story better/clearer without completely changing its direction.

I feel like so far you've set a lot of difficult challenges up for the story

I want this story to work and am willing to put in as much effort as needed by me. That being said, I really should make a draft before saying that.

Thank you so much for all your input. As i said before, even though this entire conversation might not lead to a greenlight by you, I am still very grateful for the time and thought you have given me.
Thanks again!

item.title: Re: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Took a look at the revised version. It's still too contrivedly overpowered for me to take seriously, especially given that the creator individual somehow knows so much about the Foundation without any solid in-universe reasoning to explain their knowledge. The fact that they just happen to have the means to produce anomalies that could be Thaumiel class (how would they know what Thaumiel class is? Why would they assume Foundation personnel would trust their products, let alone pay for them?) and yet their scheme is disturbed by something as mundane as a coal company just makes the entire story seem sloppily set up.

+ show block
– hide block

Material like this:

They found out about the foundation after witnessing them contain an SCP without getting noticed himself (thorough as the foundation might be) and then began to educate himself on how to make anomalies (not yet specified, more research needed).

just makes me as a reader skeptical. It's already a stretch of disbelief for me to believe that the Foundation just happened to not notice this person witnessing a containment incident (and said person just happens to have the factory means to produce anomalies somehow). When you add in the fact that they somehow learned enough about the Foundation to figure out the kind of anomalies that would be considered useful, and also created a program that can "crack open many cybersecurity features (not all) and then infect every possible device that can print", the result is a story that just feels too forced by authorial meddling to read as genuine or believable.

Why do you want to write about a factory that fails to make certain kinds of anomalies? Why Thaumiel-class items, specifically? Why do you want the factory to be the work of one person? Why do you want them to just randomly and conveniently find out a lot of information about the Foundation, thereby making the Foundation look incompetent in terms of information security?

I feel like so far you've set a lot of difficult challenges up for the story, seemingly for no other reason than you just happen to want to write things that way rather than the narrative organically developing to include those details. Most of these details are problematic because they make the story seem too fake or the main character and their creations too overpowered. How open are you to changing these elements to make the story more believable and the main character more of a relatable individual and not an excessively exceptional caricature?

item.title: Re: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your review. It is really insightful and helpful!

The first issue with this is that I have difficulty taking the Foundation response seriously. The researchers have no reason to believe that just because they found a location that produces anomalies, said anomalies will be automatically useful. It also makes me skeptical that they would immediately use said anomalies to assist the Foundation in the first place; the Foundation exists to contain anomalies first, not to put them to questionable/unreliable use. As a reader, I'm also confused as to how the researchers started running tests on the items in the first place, since the effects noted aren't really instinctive (for example, how would someone know which criteria to test to determine the specific effects of the box?).

That makes sense actually. The researchers wouldnt know anything about its anomalous effects so they probably wouldnt just throw other SCPs inside it and see what happens. They also wouldn't just use unreliable barely tested SCPs to contain others so it would never get classified as Thaumiel in the first place. I will try and figure something out to fix those issues!

+ show block
– hide block

…which brings me to the second major issue; I feel like there needs to be more explanation/worldbuilding behind why the warehouse behaves the way it does. I think we already have a Thaumiel location that knowingly assists the Foundation (I think it's a renovated schoolbuilding or the like; try using the Tag Search tool to find it), so what you have here just seems like a slight variation of it but without narrative context. Did the warehouse just spontaneously start existing to produce anomalies? Why does it want to help the Foundation at all?

I found the article in questions and yeah, they are kinda similar… What i could do to change that would be to make it non sapient and sentient and maybe not even a building… I just got a good idea of how to fix that! Will make another concept post.

Overall… I'm not convinced that this would be workable on the mainsite as currently presented. The Foundation personnel seem too quickly disappointed, and the warehouse itself seems shallowly developed. I think the first steps to take here would be to better develop the warehouse's history and motives so it exists as a meaningful character on its own, without needing the Foundation to give it significance.

Hmmm… Not too sure on how to addresse this problem. I need some time to think about a good backstory, but i get what you mean.

Thank you very much for your crit. It is really helpful!

item.title: Re: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look.

The first issue with this is that I have difficulty taking the Foundation response seriously. The researchers have no reason to believe that just because they found a location that produces anomalies, said anomalies will be automatically useful. It also makes me skeptical that they would immediately use said anomalies to assist the Foundation in the first place; the Foundation exists to contain anomalies first, not to put them to questionable/unreliable use. As a reader, I'm also confused as to how the researchers started running tests on the items in the first place, since the effects noted aren't really instinctive (for example, how would someone know which criteria to test to determine the specific effects of the box?).

…which brings me to the second major issue; I feel like there needs to be more explanation/worldbuilding behind why the warehouse behaves the way it does. I think we already have a Thaumiel location that knowingly assists the Foundation (I think it's a renovated schoolbuilding or the like; try using the Tag Search tool to find it), so what you have here just seems like a slight variation of it but without narrative context. Did the warehouse just spontaneously start existing to produce anomalies? Why does it want to help the Foundation at all?

Also, last thing, note the difference between sentient and sapient. Sentience can be attributed to animals like dogs and cats and lobsters that can perceive and react to external stimuli and feel pain; sapience is what is needed for human-level self-awareness and communication ability.

Overall… I'm not convinced that this would be workable on the mainsite as currently presented. The Foundation personnel seem too quickly disappointed, and the warehouse itself seems shallowly developed. I think the first steps to take here would be to better develop the warehouse's history and motives so it exists as a meaningful character on its own, without needing the Foundation to give it significance.

item.title: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight) (Revised)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Second Revision

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy, Emotional (might be just an emotional piece)

Page Layout: When first entering the article, you will only be able to see the part of the SCP that's dangerous i.e. the computervirus that keeps on printing out the credentials of a bankrupt business. Scrolling down you will find a "insert clearance 4/XXXX" which will reveal the factory part of the SCP which is classified as safe, potentially thaumiel

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a 2 part Anomaly: Part 1 is a computerprogram that is able to crack open many cybersecurity features (not all) and then infects every possible device that is able to physically print out a message (printer, fax machines, 3d printer). 2nd Part is a warehouse, which location is included inside the printed messages. This warehouse houses a giant machine which is able to produce anomalies that could end up as thaumiel if improved.
Efforts are ongoing to find the individual, who created this SCP.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: "Our business relationship has to come to an abruptive end before they even really began. I have no more funds to spare and only failures to sell. It has been a pleasure trying to do business." is the message getting printed out by many different devices all over germany. Attached to it are the credentials of a bankrupt business. The foundation covers this incident up and pushes updates that make the virus unable to infect more devices. The source does not get found and efforts are ongoing. The business mentioned is located on an untouched coal reserve that has been bought by a coal mining company. This factory is supposed to create thaumiel SCPs and then sell them to the foundation. This factory is supposed to tell the story of how one individual tried building up a business with this idea and how this coal company ruined them by denying them access to much needed ressources. This story and the purpose of this factory are written down in a digital form by the missing individual. All testing is halted until the mysterious individual is found. The Individual will be found and tries to improve this SCP but is unable to stop the computervirus he released. Testing logs of prototypes by said individual included.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A story of medium length of how an SCP got made without malicious intent, made to aid the foundation. Also includes testing logs by someone not from the foundation.

Additional Notes:
The individual, who made this SCP, is not anomalous in nature. They found out about the foundation after witnessing them contain an SCP without getting noticed himself (thorough as the foundation might be) and then began to educate himself on how to make anomalies (not yet specified, more research needed).
